action_categories.definition: Reads or displays existing textual content from a file or bounded region. Examples: `sed -n '1,120p' <source.c>`; `nl -ba <patch> | sed -n '20,60p'`.
exclude: Text or symbol matching as the primary operation; use SEARCH_TEXT.
Path enumeration; use LIST_PATHS or SEARCH_PATHS.
Binary-byte rendering; use DUMP_BINARY.
Version-control metadata queries; use QUERY_REPOSITORY.
include: Reading source, headers, scripts, configuration, patches, changelogs, logs, or excerpts.
Using commands whose primary effect is emitting existing text.

action_categories.definition: Enumerates files or directories in a specified tree without searching their contents. Examples: `rg --files <source-tree>`; `ls -l <build-dir>`.
exclude: Filesystem searches using name, type, or existence predicates; use SEARCH_PATHS.
Content or symbol searches; use SEARCH_TEXT.
Reading file contents; use READ_TEXT.
include: Listing directory or tree contents.
Enumerating paths without a name predicate or content predicate.

action_categories.definition: Searches the filesystem for paths, names, types, or existence conditions. Examples: `find <tree> -name '*.tab.i'`; `rg --files <tree> | rg 'fuzzer'`.
exclude: Unfiltered directory listing; use LIST_PATHS.
Searching file contents; use SEARCH_TEXT.
include: Using `find`, path filters, or filename regular expressions to locate files or directories.
Checking whether a named artifact or repository marker exists.

action_categories.definition: Searches file contents for literal text, symbols, macros, function names, or regular-expression patterns. Examples: `rg -n 'decode|malloc' <source-tree>`; `rg -n 'LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput' <tree>`.
exclude: Searching only path names; use SEARCH_PATHS.
Displaying matching file contents without a search operation; use READ_TEXT.
include: Content, source-code, API-symbol, macro, or pattern searches.
Searching generated code or build files for textual references.

action_categories.definition: Queries version-control metadata or history. Examples: `git -C <tree> status --short`; `git -C <tree> log --grep='fix'`.
exclude: Reading ordinary source or configuration files.
Creating a patch from non-version-control file variants; use GENERATE_DIFF.
include: Repository status, log, tag, diff, or history queries.
Checking for repository metadata before using version-control operations.

action_categories.definition: Renders binary input or file contents as bytes, hexadecimal, or another low-level binary representation. Examples: `od -An -tx1 -v <input.bin>`; `xxd <crash-file>`.
exclude: Measuring byte count; use MEASURE_FILE.
Creating or modifying binary input; use CONSTRUCT_TEST_INPUT or MODIFY_FILE.
Reading textual source.
include: Hex dumps and byte-level displays of binary files or inputs.
Printing raw byte sequences for inspection.

action_categories.definition: Measures a file or artifact using size or count metrics. Examples: `wc -c <input.bin>`; `wc -l <log>`.
exclude: Dumping the measured contents.
Inferring runtime or test outcomes from the measurement.
include: Byte, line, or similar size measurements.
Commands whose primary operation reports a quantitative file measure.

action_categories.definition: Waits for a period or repeatedly samples files, logs, or runtime state. Examples: `sleep 5; tail -n 4 <fuzz-log>`; a loop that periodically reads a log.
exclude: A single immediate file read without waiting; use READ_TEXT.
Launching the tested program or fuzzer; use the corresponding execution action.
include: Explicit sleeps, polling loops, or delayed log sampling.
Waiting for externally produced runtime records before inspecting them.

action_categories.definition: Configures or generates a project build with selected options, toolchains, or instrumentation settings. Examples: `cmake -S <src> -B <build> -DBUILD_FUZZERS=ON`; `meson setup <build>`.
exclude: Direct compiler or linker invocation; use COMPILE_TARGET.
Project compilation after configuration; use BUILD_PROJECT.
Merely reading build configuration.
include: Build-system setup and generation commands.
Selecting sanitizer, fuzzing, shared/static, feature, or output options during configuration.

action_categories.definition: Invokes a project-level build through its build system. Examples: `cmake --build <build>`; `ninja -C <build>`.
exclude: Only generating build files; use CONFIGURE_BUILD.
Direct compiler or linker commands for one target; use COMPILE_TARGET.
Executing an already built program.
include: Building configured project targets through CMake, Meson, Ninja, Make, or equivalent.
Compound commands whose substantive operation is a project build.

action_categories.definition: Directly compiles or links source into a target, including fuzzer, harness, or instrumented binaries. Examples: `clang -fsanitize=fuzzer,address <harness.c> <source.c> -o <target>`; `cc -c <source.c>`.
exclude: Project build-system invocations; use BUILD_PROJECT.
Executing the produced target.
Reading compiler configuration.
include: Compiler and linker invocations.
Adding sanitizer, fuzzing, tracing, or origin-tracking flags during compilation.

action_categories.definition: Runs a shell, Python, or other orchestration script. Examples: `bash -eux <prepare-script>`; `bash <runner-script> <input>`.
exclude: Reading a script; use READ_TEXT.
Directly invoking a compiled target without a script wrapper.
A dedicated validation harness invocation; use RUN_VALIDATOR when validation is primary.
include: Executing preparation, compilation, runner, validator-wrapper, or fuzzer-wrapper scripts.
Script execution where the script, rather than a directly invoked target, is the command object.

action_categories.definition: Invokes one executable, test binary, or harness directly on one input or fixture without a fuzzing loop or explicit sanitizer mode. Examples: `<decoder> <input.bin>`; `<test-binary> <fixture>`.
exclude: Explicit sanitizer or tracing execution as the salient mode; use EXECUTE_INSTRUMENTED_TARGET.
Coverage-guided or mutational fuzzing; use RUN_FUZZER.
Iteration over an input set; use REPLAY_INPUT_SET.
Official staged validation; use RUN_VALIDATOR.
include: One-shot execution of a compiled program or test target.
Direct execution used to exercise a single generated or supplied input.

action_categories.definition: Executes a target with explicit sanitizer, tracing, or runtime-instrumentation settings. Examples: `ASAN_OPTIONS=<options> <target> <input>`; `<msan-target> <crash-input>`.
exclude: Compiling with instrumentation; use COMPILE_TARGET.
Uninstrumented one-shot execution; use EXECUTE_TARGET.
A fuzzing engine as the primary operation; use RUN_FUZZER as applicable.
include: Running under ASan, MSan, UBSan, origin tracking, tracing, or equivalent explicit instrumentation.
Directly exercising an instrumented executable on a supplied input.

action_categories.definition: Launches a fuzzing engine or mutational/coverage-guided fuzzing session. Examples: `<fuzzer> -max_total_time=60 <corpus>`; `<fuzzer> -jobs=4 -workers=4 <corpus>`.
exclude: One-shot target execution; use EXECUTE_TARGET or EXECUTE_INSTRUMENTED_TARGET.
Replay of a fixed existing input set; use REPLAY_INPUT_SET.
Merely inspecting fuzz logs or corpus files.
include: Fuzzing runs with seeds, corpus directories, time limits, jobs, workers, RSS limits, or artifact directories.
Structure-aware and general-purpose fuzzing sessions.

action_categories.definition: Iterates over an existing collection of inputs and invokes a target for each member. Examples: `for f in <crash-dir>/*; do <target> <file>; done`; replaying a fixed crasher corpus.
exclude: Generating the cases during the loop; use CONSTRUCT_TEST_INPUT or RUN_TEST_MATRIX.
Coverage-guided mutation; use RUN_FUZZER.
A single input invocation.
include: Loops over crash, seed, regression, or corpus files for direct replay.
Control flow that handles each existing input individually or conditionally stops based on an observed invocation status.

action_categories.definition: Creates or populates directories and runtime settings needed for later testing, fuzzing, or validation. Examples: `mkdir -p <corpus> <artifacts>; cp <seed> <corpus>/`; `export MSAN_OPTIONS=<options>`.
exclude: The actual fuzzer or target invocation.
Building the target.
Copying a file as the main artifact operation; use COPY_FILE.
include: Creating corpus or artifact directories.
Copying seed files into a test area.
Setting sanitizer, fuzzer, or runner environment variables without executing the target.

action_categories.definition: Constructs, encodes, synthesizes, or parameterizes test data, a PoC, a compressed stream, or a fixture. Examples: a script that writes a structured image input; a loop that creates encoded streams.
examples: A loop encodes inputs across distance and length parameters
exclude: Only enumerating numeric candidates without constructing inputs; use ENUMERATE_VALUES.
Only writing an already defined file; use CREATE_FILE.
Executing generated cases; use RUN_TEST_MATRIX or EXECUTE_TARGET.
include: Hand-crafting protocol fields or compressed streams.
Generating PoCs, boundary cases, seeds, images, or other test fixtures.
Producing candidate values specifically as input data.

action_categories.definition: Enumerates or calculates a parameter space without invoking the tested target. Examples: looping over header flags satisfying a constraint; checking sample-conversion combinations.
examples: A script enumerates header flag values satisfying a modulus
A loop prints parameter combinations within a bound
exclude: Constructing actual test files or streams; use CONSTRUCT_TEST_INPUT.
Running a target for each value; use RUN_TEST_MATRIX.
Filesystem path searches.
include: Brute-force calculations, candidate-value enumeration, modular checks, and parameter-space filtering.
Exhaustive arithmetic checks whose output is values or combinations rather than target executions.

action_categories.definition: Systematically invokes a target over generated or parameterized test cases. Examples: looping over distance and length values while running a decoder; executing generated streams across boundary cases.
examples: A script generates and invokes a decoder across boundary parameters
exclude: Coverage-guided fuzzing; use RUN_FUZZER.
Replay of an existing corpus without generating cases; use REPLAY_INPUT_SET.
Only calculating candidates; use ENUMERATE_VALUES.
include: Batch probes and generated-test loops.
Focused exhaustive or combinatorial execution against a target.
Testing generated inputs under one or more target configurations.

action_categories.definition: Adds tracing, logging, probes, or other instrumentation to a source variant or temporary copy. Examples: copying `<source.c>` to `<trace.c>` and inserting match logging; adding diagnostic prints before compilation.
examples: Insert logging into a temporary source copy
Add a probe that records distance and length values
exclude: Ordinary bug-fix editing; use MODIFY_FILE.
Compiling or running the instrumented result; use COMPILE_TARGET or EXECUTE_INSTRUMENTED_TARGET.
include: Source-copy instrumentation and tracing edits.
Preparing a temporary instrumented implementation for compilation or execution.

action_categories.definition: Creates or adds a file artifact that did not previously exist at the target path. Examples: writing `<output/poc.bin>`; adding `<output/fix.patch>`.
exclude: Editing an existing file; use MODIFY_FILE.
Deleting or copying an existing file.
The semantic construction of test content; use CONSTRUCT_TEST_INPUT when content generation is primary.
include: File-change records of kind add.
Writing a new output, input, PoC, patch, or other artifact.

action_categories.definition: Edits or updates an existing file's contents. Examples: changing `<source.c>`; prepending a header to `<patch>`.
examples: Edit `<patch>` to add a diff header
exclude: Adding a new file; use CREATE_FILE.
Deleting a file; use DELETE_FILE.
Generating a comparison artifact from two variants; use GENERATE_DIFF.
include: File-change records of kind update.
Editing source, configuration, scripts, patches, or other existing text files.

action_categories.definition: Removes an existing file from the workspace or output area. Example: deleting `<output/patch.diff>`.
exclude: Replacing or updating file contents.
Removing an entire workspace when the observed action is directory cleanup rather than file deletion.
include: File-change records of kind delete.
Explicit file removal commands.

action_categories.definition: Copies an existing file or source variant to another path. Examples: `cp <crash-input> <output/input.bin>`; copying an original source before editing.
exclude: Moving or renaming without copying.
Creating new content from a generator.
Generating a diff from the copies; use GENERATE_DIFF for that operation.
include: Explicit file duplication or preservation before modification.
Copying an input or source file to an output or temporary path.

action_categories.definition: Computes or emits a unified, Git-style, or other textual difference between source variants. Examples: `diff -u <old.c> <new.c> > <patch>`; `unified_diff(<old>, <new>)`.
examples: A script prints a unified diff between two source variants
exclude: Editing an already generated patch; use MODIFY_FILE.
Applying a patch or running a validator; use RUN_VALIDATOR when that is the primary action.
Comparing repository history; use QUERY_REPOSITORY.
include: Creating a patch or diff by comparing original and modified content.
Emitting diff headers, hunks, or unified-diff text.

action_categories.definition: Invokes a dedicated validation harness over a PoC, patch, project, or test set. Examples: `<validator> --poc-file <poc> --patch-file <patch>`; a staged validation command with preparation options.
exclude: Do not classify whether validation passed, failed, was skipped, or produced a crash.
General target execution, fuzzing, or test loops without a dedicated validation harness.
include: Official or project-provided validation scripts and staged PoC/patch/test validation.
Commands that apply or assess a supplied patch as part of a validation harness.

message_roles.definition: States a future, intended, or conditional action without claiming that it has occurred. Examples: `I will inspect the harness and derive an input`; `I am going to regenerate the diff from a modified copy`.
examples: `I will inspect the harness and map the input flow.`
`I am going to regenerate the diff from the modified source.`
exclude: Current execution status; use PROGRESS_STATUS.
A completed observation or artifact report; use RESULT_REPORT or FINDING_REPORT.
An asserted cause; use HYPOTHESIS or DIAGNOSIS.
include: Plans, action announcements, investigation plans, validation plans, testing plans, and implementation plans.
Conditional future actions and declared intended scope.

message_roles.definition: Reports current activity, phase, or work state without primarily stating a new technical result. Examples: `The build is in progress`; `Validation is still in the build/run phase`.
examples: `The target build is still in progress.`
exclude: Future-only intent; use PLAN_INTENT.
Observed diagnostic or validator output; use RESULT_REPORT.
A causal explanation or discovered issue.
include: Ongoing work, current state, phase updates, and status summaries.
Statements that an activity has started, remains underway, or is ready for another activity.

message_roles.definition: Describes inspection, tracing, auditing, harness behavior, or analysis activity without asserting a definitive cause. Examples: `I am tracing the entrypoint and immediate callees`; `The harness reinterprets input as fixed-width values`.
examples: `I am tracing the entrypoint and its immediate callees.`
`The harness allocates output from an input-derived size.`
exclude: A future-only plan; use PLAN_INTENT.
A candidate explanation; use HYPOTHESIS.
A confirmed mechanism or root cause; use DIAGNOSIS.
include: Source-reading, call-path tracing, data-flow mapping, harness descriptions, and audit updates.
Reports of what area is being examined or how a harness operates.

message_roles.definition: Proposes, revises, or narrows a suspected explanation or attack surface without presenting it as established fact. Examples: `A missing upper-bound check may index a packed table`; `A malformed multi-block case may reach the copy path`.
examples: `A missing bounds check may permit an out-of-range lookup.`
`The issue may require a multi-block input.`
exclude: An asserted root cause; use DIAGNOSIS.
A deliberate pivot away from a prior candidate; use STRATEGY_REVISION.
A neutral observation without speculation.
include: Suspected bug classes, candidate vulnerable areas, tentative mechanisms, and unresolved explanations.
Statements using uncertainty or exploratory framing.

message_roles.definition: Explicitly rejects, replaces, or redirects an earlier investigative candidate or method. Examples: `The first candidate was a false lead; attention is shifting to output handling`.
examples: `The initial candidate was a false lead; I am switching to the output path.`
`The first fix was too narrow, so the fallback case is being reconsidered.`
exclude: A new tentative hypothesis without a pivot; use HYPOTHESIS.
Routine progress or debugging on the same line of inquiry.
A source-change description.
include: False-lead declarations, investigation pivots, revised approaches, and replacement strategies.
Statements that change the selected line of inquiry.

message_roles.definition: States an asserted causal mechanism, root cause, or direct explanation for an observed defect. Examples: `Compaction ignores a boundary field`; `The parser uses a pointer after the buffer has advanced`.
examples: `The merge condition ignores the boundary level.`
`The parser retains a pointer across a buffer-advancing read.`
exclude: Tentative speculation; use HYPOTHESIS.
A report that only says an issue or artifact was found; use FINDING_REPORT.
A neutral command result.
include: Bug diagnoses, root-cause reports, and causal technical explanations.
Claims that connect a code behavior to a defect mechanism.

message_roles.definition: Reports an unresolved, repeated, or unexpected symptom together with active troubleshooting of its cause or targeting. Examples: `The input still reaches the same copy site; I am checking patch targeting`.
examples: `The same copy site is still reached; patch targeting is being checked.`
`The initial trigger is not reproducing, so the input path is being narrowed.`
exclude: A confirmed causal explanation; use DIAGNOSIS.
A future-only debugging plan; use PLAN_INTENT.
A neutral final observation without troubleshooting.
include: Repeated symptoms, remaining faults, and checks of patch scope, overlap, target selection, or execution path.
Troubleshooting updates that do not yet establish a final diagnosis.

message_roles.definition: Reports an actual source, patch, instrumentation, or artifact change, including preparation of an external patch. Examples: `The payload pointer is now taken after the read`; `The fallback now copies overlapping bytes individually`.
examples: `The pointer assignment was moved after the read.`
`The fallback copy now expands overlapping data byte by byte.`
exclude: A future implementation intention without an edit; use PLAN_INTENT.
A diagnosis without a change.
A validator or test result.
include: Descriptions of edits already made or currently being applied.
Patch preparation, source-fix updates, and implementation changes.

message_roles.definition: Reports a discovered issue, location, artifact, or relevant finding as an identified result. Examples: `I found a memory-safety issue in list compaction`; `The vulnerable routine is in the parser`.
examples: `I found a memory-safety issue in the compaction logic.`
`The vulnerable routine is in the post-data parser.`
exclude: A causal root-cause explanation; use DIAGNOSIS.
A merely observed command output; use RESULT_REPORT.
A proposed or future action.
include: Finding reports that identify a bug, vulnerable area, artifact, or sanitizer location.
Summaries that connect a discovery to produced PoC or patch artifacts without explaining the full mechanism.

message_roles.definition: Reports an observed output, diagnostic, artifact state, or validation record without classifying its success or failure. Examples: `The run emitted an uninitialized-memory trace`; `The validator printed stage labels and a patch-application message`.
examples: `The run emitted a sanitizer trace at <function>.`
`The validator printed stage labels and a patch message.`
exclude: Do not encode whether a run passed, failed, crashed, or succeeded as a category.
A discovered defect or location stated as a finding; use FINDING_REPORT.
A causal explanation; use DIAGNOSIS.
include: Neutral reports of command output, sanitizer diagnostics, emitted files, stage records, or measured observations.
Reports of what was observed without adding a causal interpretation.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns the target executable, test or fuzzing harness, entry point, input representation, and calls exercised by the input. Examples: mapping bytes to library APIs; locating a fuzz entry point and immediate callees.
examples: `I am locating the fuzz entry point and mapping bytes to library calls.`
`The harness converts the input into fixed-width elements before analysis.`
exclude: Build mechanics alone; use BUILD_TOOLCHAIN_AND_INSTRUMENTATION.
Actual fuzzing or validation output.
A domain-specific root cause.
include: Harness discovery, input-to-call tracing, target scoping, and harness behavior.
Descriptions of how raw input becomes API arguments or allocated buffers.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns configuring, compiling, building, instrumenting, or making a target available, including sanitizer toolchains. Examples: a local memory-instrumented build; compiler flags for a fuzz target.
examples: `The target is being rebuilt with memory instrumentation.`
`The compiler flags are being checked for the fuzz harness.`
exclude: The behavior of the target after execution.
A source-level defect mechanism.
A fuzzing corpus or sanitizer diagnostic itself.
include: Build progress, compiler configuration, sanitizer/fuzzer flags, target availability, and local build setup.
Plans or reports about building a target before exercising it.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns fuzzing sessions, seed or crasher corpora, parallel fuzzing, corpus artifacts, and replay of existing inputs. Examples: replaying historical crash files; examining fuzzing logs or corpus growth.
examples: `The existing crasher corpus is being replayed against the current target.`
`The fuzz logs and seed corpus are under inspection.`
exclude: Deriving or minimizing one PoC; use CRASH_INPUT_AND_POC.
A one-shot sanitizer diagnostic; use MEMORY_SAFETY_DIAGNOSTICS.
Compiler/build setup.
include: Fuzzing strategy, corpus preparation, fuzz logs, historical crash inputs, and replay behavior.
Parallel jobs, time limits, seed sets, and crasher-corpus checks.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns deriving, minimizing, selecting, reproducing, or packaging a crashing input or proof-of-concept artifact. Examples: reducing a sanitizer-triggering input; writing a PoC file.
examples: `I have a small crashing input and am minimizing it into a PoC.`
`The trigger input was written as an external artifact.`
exclude: The sanitizer diagnostic itself; use MEMORY_SAFETY_DIAGNOSTICS.
Patch mechanics; use PATCH_CONSTRUCTION_AND_APPLICATION.
Validator stage execution; use VALIDATION_EXECUTION.
include: Crash-input derivation, minimization, PoC candidates, PoC artifacts, and the relation between an input and a trigger.
Historical inputs when discussed as candidate PoCs rather than corpus operations.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns sanitizer findings and memory-safety manifestations such as uninitialized reads, out-of-bounds access, use-after-free, or exact diagnostic locations. Examples: an MSan trace; an ASan report tied to a function.
examples: `The instrumented run reports uninitialized memory at <function>.`
`The sanitizer location was mapped back to the decompressor.`
exclude: A confirmed code-level root cause; use DIAGNOSIS with the relevant subject.
General build instrumentation; use BUILD_TOOLCHAIN_AND_INSTRUMENTATION.
A PoC artifact without diagnostic content; use CRASH_INPUT_AND_POC.
include: ASan, MSan, UBSan, origin-tracking, memory-safety, and sanitizer-location discussion.
Observed or anticipated memory-safety behavior.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns compressed-data formats and decoder state, including zlib or deflate headers, fixed or dynamic Huffman coding, code-length expansion, symbol validity, and multi-block edge cases. Examples: testing header flags; reviewing invalid distance symbols.
examples: `A malformed distance symbol is being examined.`
`The dynamic code-length expansion may exceed its state storage.`
exclude: Backreference overlap, fast-copy, or output-buffer bounds; use DECOMPRESSION_COPY_OUTPUT_BOUNDS.
Generic sanitizer diagnostics.
Build or harness setup.
include: Compressed-stream construction, protocol header fields, Huffman tables, dynamic code lengths, invalid symbols, and decoder-state transitions.
Boundary cases whose main subject is encoded-data interpretation.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns decompressor output limits and match-copy behavior, including backreference overlap, fast paths, fallback copies, match-source materialization, and output-buffer bounds. Examples: bytewise copying for overlap; tracing distance and counter values.
examples: `The fallback must copy an overlapping match one byte at a time.`
`The investigation is tracing match distance, length, and output offsets.`
exclude: Huffman symbol decoding when copy behavior is not involved; use DECOMPRESSION_ENCODING_AND_STATE.
General sanitizer reporting without decompression-copy content.
Patch formatting or pathing as such; use PATCH_CONSTRUCTION_AND_APPLICATION.
include: Backreference copy loops, output paths, buffer bounds, overlap conditions, and fast/fallback copy behavior.
Tracing or fixing the source of copied match bytes.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns buffer advancement, read callbacks, stale pointers, and the lifetime or timing of payload pointers across parser reads. Examples: acquiring a payload pointer after a read advances the buffer; auditing a callback-based reader.
examples: `The payload pointer must be taken after the read advances the buffer.`
`The reader callback and pointer lifetime are being audited.`
exclude: Chunk order or metadata semantics without pointer-lifetime content; use IMAGE_CHUNK_METADATA_PARSING.
Decompressor match-copy pointers; use DECOMPRESSION_COPY_OUTPUT_BOUNDS.
Generic source inspection.
include: Pointer validity across reads, buffer-mode parsing, read callbacks, payload-pointer acquisition, and stale-pointer fixes.
Parser state that changes when a read consumes bytes.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns image-container chunk parsing, ancillary metadata, chunk order, post-data validation, CRC or header checks, and metadata-specific parser paths. Examples: a metadata chunk after image data; validating ancillary chunks.
examples: `A metadata chunk after image data is being used as a parser trigger.`
`The post-data ancillary-chunk validation path is under review.`
exclude: Pixel conversion, row filters, or decoded-output sizing; use IMAGE_DECODE_PIXEL_CONVERSION.
Pointer lifetime as the primary topic; use PARSER_POINTER_LIFETIME.
Generic binary input generation.
include: Chunk readers, post-data or post-IDAT validation, metadata chunks, chunk ordering, and parser callbacks when image-container semantics are central.
Input construction involving ancillary metadata.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns image decoding, decoded-output sizing, pixel sample normalization, gamma or ancillary transforms, scanlines, row filters, and optimized pixel paths. Examples: computing RGBA output size; brute-checking sample conversion combinations.
examples: `The harness computes RGBA output size before decoding.`
`Sample normalization and row-filter combinations are being checked.`
exclude: Chunk parsing and pointer lifetime; use IMAGE_CHUNK_METADATA_PARSING or PARSER_POINTER_LIFETIME.
Generic fuzzer build or execution.
Unrelated binary input construction.
include: Image decode harness behavior, pixel-format conversion, gamma/sample scaling, row filters, SIMD paths, and output allocation.
Focused tests of pixel conversion or decoded image size.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns generated or packed lookup tables, generated macros, Unicode or code-point bounds, and table-generator behavior. Examples: checking whether an out-of-range code point indexes a packed table; locating generated table bodies.
examples: `A raw code point may index a packed table without an upper bound.`
`The generated lookup macro bodies are being located.`
exclude: Linked-list or run compaction; use LINKED_LIST_COMPACTION_BOUNDARIES.
General generated build artifacts without lookup semantics.
A generic API search with no table or Unicode subject.
include: Unicode and bracket lookup tables, generated includes, packed-table macros, code-generation sources, and bounds around table indexing.
Hypotheses about raw code points bypassing table bounds.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns linked-list or run-list mutation, compaction, adjacent-node merging, isolate or boundary bookkeeping, and resulting stale or freed-node references. Examples: merging adjacent runs without respecting a boundary field.
examples: `Compaction merges adjacent nodes without respecting a boundary field.`
`The adjacent-node lookup follows a stale link after list mutation.`
exclude: Generated Unicode lookup tables; use GENERATED_TABLES_AND_UNICODE_LOOKUPS.
Generic allocator or sanitizer discussion without list content.
Parser pointer lifetime.
include: List construction, compaction conditions, adjacent-node lookup, boundary levels, isolate/bracket bookkeeping, and list memory safety.
Root-cause or fix discussions centered on list mutation.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns designing, generating, formatting, targeting, pathing, applying, or packaging a source patch. Examples: repository-relative diff paths; regenerating a patch from an exact modified copy.
examples: `The patch is being regenerated from the exact modified source copy.`
exclude: Running the dedicated validator as an operation; use VALIDATION_EXECUTION.
The underlying bug mechanism without patch content.
A PoC input without patch content.
include: Fix strategy expressed as a patch, diff formatting, patch headers, context, target paths, application mechanics, and external patch artifacts.
Patch-specific overlap or targeting discussions.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns invoking or reporting on a dedicated validator and its PoC, patch, preparation, or test stages. Examples: running a validator with a PoC and patch; recording stage labels.
examples: `The validator is being run with a PoC and patch.`
`Validation output contains stage labels and a patch-application record.`
exclude: Do not encode pass, fail, crash, or success as a subject category.
General fuzzing or corpus replay; use FUZZING_CORPUS_AND_REPLAY.
Patch formatting/pathing without validator execution; use PATCH_CONSTRUCTION_AND_APPLICATION.
include: Official validation harness execution, PoC validation, patch validation, and validation-stage status.
Statements about validation being underway or about validator-emitted records.

message_subjects.definition: Concerns repository history, version-control provenance, differential comparison, alternate local copies, packages, caches, or historical fixes. Examples: searching local history for a fix; comparing an alternate source copy.
examples: `The source tree lacks history, so a cached alternate copy is being compared.`
`Local repository history is being searched for a prior fix.`
exclude: Current source or build inspection without provenance content.
Creating or applying the current patch; use PATCH_CONSTRUCTION_AND_APPLICATION.
General filesystem search unrelated to reference comparison.
include: Git history/status/tag investigations, differential analysis, local package lookup, and alternate-version comparison.
Searching provenance artifacts because the active tree lacks history.

object_categories.definition: A project source checkout or source directory tree treated as a collection. Examples: `<src-tree>`; a command listing files under `<source-tree>`.
exclude: A configured build workspace; use BUILD_TREE.
A generic output or temporary directory; use DIRECTORY_PATH.
A single source file; use SOURCE_CODE or HEADER_INTERFACE.
include: Directories containing implementation, header, test, generator, or documentation sources.
Source-tree paths used for recursive listing or searching.

object_categories.definition: A configured or generated build workspace and its inventory. Examples: `<build-dir>`; a command inspecting generated build artifacts.
exclude: Declarative build definitions as individual files; use BUILD_CONFIGURATION.
A single executable; use EXECUTABLE_TARGET.
A source checkout.
include: Build directories, generated build metadata, and build-tree inventories.
Temporary configured workspaces used to locate compiled or generated outputs.

object_categories.definition: An implementation source file, source excerpt, numbered region, or source variant. Examples: `<decoder.c>`; lines from `<parser.c>`.
exclude: Headers or API declarations; use HEADER_INTERFACE.
Build files or scripts.
Generated lookup/codegen output; use GENERATED_CODE_TABLE.
Patch files; use PATCH_DIFF.
include: C, C++, or other implementation files and their excerpts.
Temporary modified copies of implementation source.

object_categories.definition: A public or internal header, declaration file, type-definition file, or API interface. Examples: `<library.h>`; `<internal-types.h>`.
exclude: Implementation source files.
Build configuration and scripts.
Generated tables unless the header is the generated artifact itself.
include: Headers containing declarations, macros, types, constants, or API definitions.
Interface excerpts searched or displayed as code.

object_categories.definition: A declarative build-system file or build option set. Examples: `<CMakeLists.txt>`; `<meson.build>`; `<build-cache>`.
exclude: A script that orchestrates commands; use SCRIPT.
A materialized build workspace; use BUILD_TREE.
Runtime or validator configuration; use PROJECT_CONFIGURATION.
include: CMake, Meson, Make, Ninja, or equivalent build definitions and options.
Build caches or configuration fragments when inspected as build configuration.

object_categories.definition: An executable shell, Python, or similar orchestration script. Examples: `<prepare-script>`; `<runner-script>`; `<validator-wrapper>`.
exclude: A build definition file; use BUILD_CONFIGURATION.
A fuzzer harness source file; use TEST_HARNESS.
A compiled executable.
include: Preparation, compilation, runner, fuzzing, and validation scripts as files or command objects.
Scripts read, executed, or searched as script text.

object_categories.definition: Source for a test or fuzzing harness, including its entry point and input-to-library wiring. Examples: `<fuzzer-harness.c>`; `<reader-test.cc>`.
exclude: Production implementation source.
A compiled harness binary; use EXECUTABLE_TARGET.
A runner script; use SCRIPT.
include: Fuzzer entrypoint source, test harness source, and harness-specific glue.
Harness files that allocate buffers, decode inputs, or call library APIs.

object_categories.definition: A compiled executable, test binary, fuzzer, sanitizer binary, or tracing binary. Examples: `<fuzzer>`; `<decoder-asan>`; `<trace-target>`.
exclude: Source for the executable; use SOURCE_CODE or TEST_HARNESS.
An input file passed to the executable; use INPUT_DATA.
A build directory containing the executable; use BUILD_TREE.
include: Built programs invoked directly or through scripts.
Instrumented and non-instrumented executables.

object_categories.definition: One raw input or fixture supplied to a target. Examples: `<poc.bin>`; `<crash-input>`; a compressed stream; a structured image.
exclude: A collection of inputs; use CORPUS.
A patch or diff; use PATCH_DIFF.
A source or executable.
include: PoCs, crash inputs, seed files, generated streams, images, null-byte inputs, and individual regression fixtures.
Raw byte sequences treated as one target input.

object_categories.definition: A collection or directory of seed, fuzzing, regression, or crasher inputs. Examples: `<seed-corpus>`; `<crasher-dir>`.
exclude: A single input file; use INPUT_DATA.
A log collection; use LOG_RECORD.
A generic output directory with unrelated artifacts.
include: Directories or sets containing multiple test inputs.
Fuzzing corpora and historical crasher collections.

object_categories.definition: A runtime, fuzzing, sanitizer, tracing, or validation log or log excerpt. Examples: `<fuzz.log>`; a sanitizer trace; a tail of runtime output.
exclude: Source code that contains logging statements.
A single input or artifact file.
A command's result when no log object is being inspected.
include: Persistent logs and diagnostic traces read or tailed as records.
Runtime output treated as a log object rather than source text.

object_categories.definition: A patch, unified diff, Git-style diff, or patch artifact. Examples: `<fix.diff>`; `<patch-file>`.
exclude: The modified source itself; use SOURCE_CODE.
A PoC or test input; use INPUT_DATA.
Repository history queries.
include: Patch files, diff text, diff hunks, and patch variants.
Artifacts intended to modify source through a textual change.

object_categories.definition: Generated source, amalgamated source, packed lookup table, generated include, or code-generation output. Examples: `<generated-table.i>`; `<amalgamated.c>`.
exclude: The generator implementation; use SOURCE_CODE.
Declarative build configuration.
A generic source file with no generated status.
include: Generated Unicode or protocol tables, packed macros, amalgamated files, and generated includes.
Outputs of code generators inspected as generated artifacts.

object_categories.definition: Version-control metadata or records describing repository history and state. Examples: `<tree>/.git`; status, tag, or log metadata.
exclude: Ordinary source-tree contents.
An external package or alternate source copy; use REFERENCE_ARTIFACT.
include: Repository directories, commit history, tags, status records, and version-control state.
Metadata queried to locate prior fixes or determine repository availability.

object_categories.definition: Runtime, validator, immutable-file, or project-level configuration distinct from build configuration. Examples: `<validator-config>`; `<runtime-config>`.
exclude: Compiler/build options; use BUILD_CONFIGURATION.
A shell/Python orchestration file; use SCRIPT.
A source file.
include: TOML, YAML, JSON, or similar files defining validation targets, runtime settings, or project policy.
Configuration identifying a repository target or protected paths.

object_categories.definition: A generic directory or path whose semantic type is not more specific. Examples: `<output-dir>`; `<temporary-dir>`; `<backup-path>`.
exclude: Source trees, build trees, and corpora when those roles are explicit.
A specific file object.
include: Output, temporary, backup, artifact, or configuration directories treated as paths.
Path arguments without a source-tree, build-tree, corpus, or other specific role.

object_categories.definition: A search target consisting of symbols, identifiers, macros, function names, literals, or regular-expression patterns. Examples: `decode_image`; `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`; `malloc|memcpy`.
exclude: The source file containing the symbol.
A generated table artifact when it is the searched file rather than the pattern.
include: API symbols, generated macro names, source patterns, and search expressions.
Names searched across files rather than files themselves.

object_categories.definition: Project documentation or explanatory text that is not source, configuration, or a runtime log. Examples: `<CHANGELOG>`; `<README>`.
exclude: Source code, headers, scripts, and logs.
A diagnostic message emitted by a command.
include: Changelogs, readmes, design notes, and similar documentation files.

object_categories.definition: An external, cached, packaged, or alternate local artifact used for comparison or provenance. Examples: `<package-cache>`; `<alternate-source-copy>`; `<archive>`.
exclude: The active source tree or build tree.
A generated patch or current output artifact.
include: Local packages, tarballs, cached copies, installed artifacts, and alternate source versions.
Artifacts searched to find historical fixes or compare implementations.

object_categories.definition: A deliberately grouped set of heterogeneous output artifacts. Examples: a PoC together with a patch; an output directory containing both.
examples: A bundle of generated validation artifacts
exclude: A homogeneous input corpus; use CORPUS.
A single patch or input.
A project source or build tree.
include: Commands that treat multiple generated deliverables as one bundle.
Grouped PoC, patch, report, or output-artifact references.
